explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full vaultkey system, prioritizing the primary settings/privacy flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Vaultkey site suffers from significant UX issues that undermine user trust and task completion, particularly on mobile. Critical problems include broken interactive components like the FAQ accordion, misleading pricing states, and non-functional navigation links that act as dead ends. Mobile usability is severely compromised by undersized tap targets and horizontal overflow, making core interactions like the Business seat slider highly frustrating.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the Vaultkey marketing and pricing system, focusing on interactive pricing components, navigation, responsive layout shifts, and accessibility of controls.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will start by exploring the landing page (index.html), validating navigation, layout, and mobile responsiveness. It will then transition to the pricing page (pricing.html) to deeply test the billing toggle, the Business per-seat slider/input, and the FAQ accordion. Finally, it will verify the feature comparison table and ensure all critical states are checked on both desktop and mobile viewports.
assumptions: The site is a static front-end with no backend, so form submissions and authentication flows will not actually process.
The Business per-seat slider and number input are bi-directionally linked and should update the price dynamically.
The FAQ accordion expands and collapses sections without routing to a new page.
Navigation links pointing to '#' (Security, Enterprise, Help, Sign in, Get Vaultkey, Download free) will not navigate away but may trigger anchor scrolls or no-ops.
risk_hotspots: Business per-seat slider and linked number input synchronization (pricing.html)
Yearly/Monthly billing toggle state and price recalculation across all plans (pricing.html)
Small tap targets for navigation links identified in the prescan (especially on mobile viewports)
FAQ accordion keyboard accessibility and state management (pricing.html)
Feature comparison table readability and horizontal scrolling on mobile viewports (pricing.html)

findings.user_goal: Learn more about product details and policies
findings.problem: The FAQ accordion items fail to expand or provide visual feedback when clicked, leaving users unable to access the information.
findings.evidence: Clicking FAQ items like 'Is the Personal plan really free forever?', 'Do passkeys work everywhere?', and 'How does Business billing work?' resulted in no visible text change, no content expansion, and the '▼' indicator failing to update to '▲'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users rely on FAQs to answer critical trust and billing questions; broken accordions block information retrieval and make the site appear unresponsive or broken.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the JavaScript for the FAQ accordion correctly toggles an 'active' class to expand the content and rotate the arrow indicator. Provide a fallback or ensure event listeners are properly attached.

findings.problem: The Family plan displays 'Billed yearly' text even when the Monthly billing toggle is active, and the Business plan yearly total does not reflect the advertised 20% annual discount.
findings.evidence: When the Monthly toggle is active, the Family plan still shows 'Billed yearly'. Additionally, the Business plan yearly total calculates to $1006.56 (12 * $6.99 * 12), which is exactly 12 times the monthly rate with no annual discount applied.
findings.why_it_matters: Inconsistent and mathematically incorrect pricing erodes user trust and creates confusion about how much they will actually be charged, potentially leading to cart abandonment.
findings.suggestion: Update the DOM to dynamically change 'Billed yearly' to 'Billed monthly' when the toggle is switched. Ensure the yearly total calculation applies the 20% discount consistently across all plans.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the site and configure pricing on a mobile device
findings.problem: Interactive elements, including navigation links, CTAs, billing toggles, and the Business seat slider, have tap targets well below the 44px minimum mobile guideline.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flagged 'Sign in' (44x16px), 'Help' (30x30px), 'Get Vaultkey' CTA (125x34px), billing toggles (153x32px, 90x32px), and the Business seat slider (16px height).
findings.why_it_matters: Undersized tap targets cause accidental mis-taps, frustration, and make precise interactions—like dragging the seat slider—nearly impossible for mobile users.
findings.suggestion: Increase padding on nav links, CTAs, and toggles to meet the 44x44px minimum touch target size. For the slider, increase the track height or use a larger custom thumb hitbox.
findings.source_hint: pricing.html, index.html header and interactive controls

findings.user_goal: Sign up or get started with the product
findings.problem: Primary CTAs and navigation links are non-functional placeholder links that lead to dead ends.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Get Personal', 'Get Vaultkey', 'Talk to sales →', 'Help', and 'Security' only appends '#' to the URL with no visible navigation, modal, or feedback.
findings.why_it_matters: Dead-end links on primary conversion paths prevent users from completing their goals (signing up, contacting sales, getting help) and make the product feel unfinished.
findings.suggestion: Replace '#' hrefs with proper destination pages, or implement modals/inline forms for actions like 'Talk to sales'. At a minimum, add visual feedback or a 'Coming soon' state.

findings.user_goal: Configure Business plan seats using assistive technology
findings.problem: The Business plan seat number input lacks a proper label, aria-label, or placeholder, and its accessible name fails to update dynamically.
findings.evidence: The number input was flagged as having no label, aria-label, or placeholder. Additionally, after changing the value to 192, the input's 'name' attribute in the DOM summary remained '12'.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will not know the purpose of the input, nor will they be informed of value changes, completely blocking them from configuring the Business plan pricing.
findings.suggestion: Add a visible <label> element associated with the input, or an aria-label like 'Number of seats'. Ensure ARIA live regions or attribute updates announce value changes to assistive technologies.

findings.user_goal: View pricing details and feature comparisons on mobile
findings.problem: The page content overflows the mobile viewport, causing horizontal scrolling and layout issues.
findings.evidence: On a 390px mobile viewport, the page width was detected as 395px. Feature comparison table text was truncated ('VAULT & SYNC Unlimited p'), indicating poor mobile readability.
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal overflow disrupts reading flow, makes data tables hard to comprehend, and interferes with vertical scrolling and drag interactions (like the seat slider).
findings.suggestion: Ensure all container elements use responsive CSS (e.g., max-width: 100%, overflow-x: auto for tables). Convert the feature comparison table to a stacked or accordion layout on mobile.

findings.user_goal: Understand the open/closed state of FAQ items
findings.problem: The FAQ accordion arrow indicator does not visually update to reflect the expanded state.
findings.evidence: Even when an FAQ item successfully expanded (e.g., 'Can I move my vault from another password manager?'), the arrow indicator remained a '▼' instead of changing to '▲'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users rely on visual cues to understand UI state; a static arrow fails to communicate that an item is open, leading to confusion and potential redundant clicks.
findings.suggestion: Use CSS transforms (e.g., rotate(180deg)) on the arrow icon when the accordion item receives an 'active' or 'open' class.
